summary: A little-documented tower near El Morro National Monument, listed as standing by FFLA but unregistered with NHLR or FFLOS.

facts.agency: Cibola National Forest (Mount Taylor Ranger District, inferred from location)

corrections.why: The FFLA list gives county 'Valencia', but the coordinates (35.04229, -108.31338) sit a few miles from El Morro National Monument, which Wikipedia places in Cibola County, New Mexico; Cibola County was carved out of the historical Valencia County area, and the FFLA record for this tower may not have been updated.

evidence.supports: El Morro landmark description, ancient trail, inscriptions
evidence.quote: Located on an ancient east–west trail in the western part of the state, the monument preserves the remains of a large prehistoric pueblo atop a great sandstone promontory with a pool of water at its base, which subsequently became a landmark where over the centuries explorers and travelers have left personal inscriptions that survive today.

evidence.supports: El Morro National Monument is in Cibola County
evidence.quote: El Morro National Monument is a U.S. national monument in Cibola County, New Mexico, United States.

evidence.supports: FFLA record: tower, standing, Valencia county, coordinates

evidence.quote: The Mount Taylor Ranger District manages land in northern Cibola, southern McKinley, and western Sandoval counties in western New Mexico.

notes_for_editor: Extremely thin sourcing: the only record found anywhere of this specific tower is one row in the FFLA's New Mexico list (name, county, coordinates, type=Tower, status=Standing, no NHLR/FFLOS link). Two WebSearch queries turned up nothing else specific to this lookout -- only material about the unrelated El Morro National Monument (the inscription rock) and general Cibola National Forest background, used here only for geographic context. No builder, construction year, design, staffing, or fate is documented anywhere I could find. The county field (Valencia) looks stale given the site's proximity to Cibola County; flagged as a correction, not applied. Confidence is low and the story is short by necessity -- a human researcher with access to Forest Service district records or an on-the-ground FFLA volunteer could likely find much more.
